name: Turso Database (Limbo)
tagline: Ground-up Rust rewrite of SQLite with concurrent writes, async I/O, CDC and vector search.
description: Turso Database, which began in late 2024 as the Limbo project, is an in-process SQL database written in Rust that aims for full SQLite compatibility (file format, SQL dialect and C API) while adding what SQLite lacks: MVCC with BEGIN CONCURRENT for parallel writers, io_uring-based asynchronous I/O, change data capture, encryption at rest, vector functions and Tantivy-powered full-text search. Its bytecode VM is designed to host multiple frontends, and a PostgreSQL dialect and wire-protocol frontend is now in development. Turso recommends it for new projects and is building its cloud around it, but it is still pre-1.0, so treat production use as early-adopter territory.

pricing.notes: Engine is MIT; Turso Cloud offers hosted sync with a free tier.

scale.notes: In-process engine; sync to Turso Cloud for replication.

strengths: BEGIN CONCURRENT MVCC allows multiple concurrent writers, unlike SQLite
Memory-safe Rust codebase with deterministic simulation testing
Asynchronous I/O (io_uring) suited to modern servers and the browser
Built-in CDC, encryption and full-text search without extensions
weaknesses: Pre-1.0: compatibility gaps and on-disk format changes are still possible
useCases: New embedded/edge apps that want SQLite plus concurrent writes
Local-first apps syncing to Turso Cloud
On-device vector search for AI features
notIdealFor: Mission-critical production systems needing proven stability today
Apps depending on niche SQLite extensions
